W|1|rule|**In one glance** Dassonville (Case 8/74, para 5): "all trading rules enacted by Member States which are capable of hindering, directly or indirectly, actually or potentially, intra-Community trade are to be considered as measures having an effect equivalent to quantitative restrictions". Keck (Joined Cases C-267/91 and C-268/91, para 16): "contrary to what has previously been decided" certain selling arrangements fall outside that formula.

W|2|rule|**In one glance** Van Gend en Loos (Case 26/62, ECR English special edition p. 1): "a new legal order of international law". Costa v ENEL (Case 6/64, ECR English special edition p. 585): the Treaty's own legal system "became an integral part of the legal systems of the Member States". Marshall (Case 152/84, para 48): "a directive may not of itself impose obligations on an individual".
